newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH STRIKER CITKO NOT TO SIGN BLACKBURN DEAL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH STRIKER CITKO NOT TO SIGN BLACKBURN DEAL.

text.p: Polish striker Marek Citko said on Tuesday he would not join English premier league side Blackburn Rovers after weeks of speculation that he might be sold for a record sum of about $6.4 million.
Citko, the star of Poland's champions Widzew Lodz, said personal issues had prevented him from going to England, as had his vow to Polish fans that he would keep on playing in Poland.
"I am staying in Widzew. I want to play here in the club to which I owe so much," the deeply religious Citko told a news conference after returning from negotiations in Blackburn.
"I am not concerned with financial matters and I want to help my club win the championship and the cup," he added.
Widzew president Andrzej Pawelec told the conference he fully understood Citko's decision. "Widzew can afford not to sell Citko," he added.

He confirmed that deals worth between 2.6 million and four million pounds sterling ($4.2 million and $6.4 million) had been discussed in England but declined to say whether talks had been held only with Blackburn.
Citko said his contract with Widzew expired after the spring league season but he wanted to extend it.
Citko grabbed the attention of talent scouts after scoring the opening goal in Poland's World Cup qualifier against England at Wembley on October 9 last year, although England went on to win 2-1.
Citko also scored two goals for Widzew in this year's Champions' League, but the Polish champions failed to qualify for next spring's quarter-final.
